clue.text: Don't leave any more in this dire shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a chaotic mess, so the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a filthy, chaotic house and vows not to leave it to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' is the anagram signal: IN THIS DIRE rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to cut someone out of a will, so you no longer leave them anything.

clue.text: Dee river in evening light

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: The River Dee seen in the evening glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dee' looks like the river but is the letter's name; the river is the Usk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the dim light of late evening, as day fades.

clue.text: Parasite, small foul-smelling one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to pong is British slang for to stink, so a ponger is something that stinks

explanation.surface: A description of a tiny, smelly bug or worm.
explanation.walkthrough: Pong is everyday British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off other people's generosity, like a social parasite.

clue.text: Shark tracks fish where small fry are gathered

parts.note: the nurse shark is a species of shark
RY is short for railway, a set of tracks
a school is a shoal of fish

explanation.surface: A shark follows the trail of fish to where young fish gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small fry' are young children, not baby fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery school is where very young children are brought together before primary school.

clue.text: One increasing volume direct from procurer

parts.note: ex means straight from, as in 'ex works'
a pander is a pimp or procurer

explanation.surface: A device that pumps up sound, bought straight from a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex works' is the trade phrase for goods sold direct from the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: An expander is anything that makes something larger, swelling its size.

clue.text: Air translated TV panel game from Middle East

indicators.note: translation changes a word into another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: QI is a British TV comedy quiz show

explanation.surface: A TV quiz show broadcast on air in translation from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges AIR; QI is a long-running BBC panel quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern country, so an Iraqi person or thing comes from there.

clue.text: Case of rowing records being overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is turned over, so the word for records is read backwards

parts.note: taps are recordings made by bugging a telephone

explanation.surface: A rowing race's results are overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' looks like the sport with oars but rhymes with 'cowing': a quarrel. 'being overturned' reverses TAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a single instance of people having a row.

clue.text: Partnership has runs in it, that is plain

indicators.note: the word for partnership has something put within it
in it says the abbreviation goes inside the word for partnership

parts.note: a pair is a partnership of two, as in cricket
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A cricket batting partnership has scored some runs, and that's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' is the flat grassland, not 'obvious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland in North America.

clue.text: He toiled to reset instrument

indicators.note: resetting puts things in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A man worked hard to recalibrate a device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' rearranges HE TOILED TO; 'to' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is a surveyor's instrument for measuring angles.

clue.text: Polish Conservative, outwardly disagreeable

indicators.note: the word for disagreeable sits on the outside, wrapping round the abbreviation

parts.note: a sour person is disagreeable and bad-tempered

explanation.surface: A Polish right-wing politician who seems unpleasant on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be a nationality; it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to clean or rub a surface hard until it shines.

clue.text: After scene, call for deal or settle perhaps using initial capital?

definitions.text: deal or settle perhaps using initial capital?

indicators.note: the word for call is placed after the word for scene

parts.note: a scene is the place where something happens
to call something is to name it

explanation.surface: A business-like note about finishing a deal or settling up using the money first invested.
explanation.walkthrough: With capitals, Deal (in Kent) and Settle (in North Yorkshire) are English towns; 'initial capital' means a capital first letter, not seed money.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like Deal and Settle, capitalised, are the names of towns, so they are examples of these.

clue.text: Accommodating bore with extremely high rental

parts.note: eager is a variant spelling of eagre, a tidal bore on a river
top means highest
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: Someone tiresome offers a room at a sky-high rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person; it is a tidal wave up a river, spelt EAGRE or EAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An accommodating person is obliging, keen to keep others happy.

clue.text: Politician identified as capable of promoting growth

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party
to finger someone is to identify them, as to the police

explanation.surface: A politician has been named as someone able to boost the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' suggests the economy, but it is plants in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A green-fingered person is a skilled gardener, good at making plants thrive.

clue.text: In new form, since I'm not comprehensively educated?

indicators.note: a new form is a different arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A pupil in a new class complains of not being well taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like a school class but signals an anagram of SINCE I'M NOT; a comprehensive is also a type of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Being omniscient means knowing everything, as if taught in every subject.

clue.text: Old Queen having radical leader of Trotskyites imprisoned and punished for beliefs

indicators.note: the queen's name has a letter placed within it
the letter is locked inside the queen's name, as a prisoner in a cell

parts.note: Mary was a Queen of England, e.g. Mary I

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a Red is a radical left-winger

explanation.surface: A historical queen jails a revolutionary Trotskyist leader and persecutes people for their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'imprisoned' are split by other words but together signal the insertion; 'radical' is a noun here, a Red.
explanation.definitionFit: To be martyred is to be killed or made to suffer for one's faith or convictions.

clue.text: Blair's alternative source of oil

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
oil is drawn from a well

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's other option for a supply of oil, a nod to Middle East policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is not Tony but Eric Blair, whose pen name was George Orwell; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the writer Eric Arthur Blair.

clue.text: Note the broadcast about large fundraiser

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation
broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An instruction to take note of a big charity appeal on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges NOTE THE; 'about' puts L inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long TV broadcast appealing for charity donations.

clue.text: It could be cricket devotee's location?

definitions.meaning: a cricket is an example of a type of small creature with six legs
read as two words, a devotee is found in a sect

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on where a fan of the game of cricket might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' is the chirping creature, not the British bat-and-ball game; split the answer IN SECT for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Crickets are jumping six-legged creatures, an example of the class.

clue.text: Entertainment from crosswords? How bizarre!

indicators.note: the answer is taken out from inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A surprised reaction to finding entertainment in a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points inside crosswordS HOW BIZarre.
explanation.definitionFit: Showbiz is the entertainment industry.

clue.text: Raid netting academic who's out for a good time

definitions.text: who's out for a good time

indicators.note: the raid word catches the academic inside it, as a net does

parts.note: a heist is a robbery or raid
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A police raid catches a university lecturer who was out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'netting' is the insertion signal; a don is the traditional Oxbridge word for a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for pleasure, always seeking enjoyment.

clue.text: Words of journalist flashing credentials to create effect

definitions.meaning: a reporter showing a pass might say '...'

explanation.surface: A reporter shows a press card to get attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I'M PRESS for the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to make a strong impression on someone.

clue.text: Pupils progressing together with speed get help completing circuit

parts.note: in Britain a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
a clip is a pace, as in 'at a fair clip'

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren walking briskly together manage to get round a lap of a track.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is the British name for a line of schoolchildren walking two by two; the circuit is electrical, not a running track.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile clip is a sprung metal clamp used to make a temporary electrical connection.

clue.text: Fool wasting time on central Colombian dialect

indicators.note: wasting loses something, so the abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

indicators.note: central means the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fool loafing around while speaking a Colombian dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Colombian has nine letters, so its central letter is M.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a form of language particular to a people or region.

clue.text: I don't know what will get me through security

definitions.meaning: in a quiz, saying '...' means you don't know the answer

definitions.text: what will get me through security

explanation.surface: Someone unsure what document will get them past the guards.
explanation.definitionFit: In a quiz 'pass' admits ignorance; a pass is also a permit for entry.

clue.text: Decorate space in style of something hanging in church?

parts.note: an em is a printer's space
a bell hangs in a church tower
the suffix -ish means 'in the manner of'

explanation.surface: Advice on adorning a room in the manner of a church furnishing.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is the printer's space as wide as the letter M, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to adorn or add ornament to something.

clue.text: Venue taking a long time to make comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A concert hall takes ages to recover its popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make comeback' reverses AN ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a large venue for sport or concerts.

clue.text: State of agitation seeing return of s-spot

indicators.note: a return goes back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: the stammered 's-spot' asks for a stammered spot: a spot is a zit, so stammering gives Z-ZIT

explanation.surface: Someone so flustered by the reappearance of a pimple that they stammer over the word.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 's-spot' is copied onto the synonym: Z-ZIT, which 'return of' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tizz, or tizzy, is a nervous, flustered state.

clue.text: A staggeringly insane sum for assistant

indicators.note: something staggering reels about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An outrageously large salary paid to a helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggeringly' rearranges INSANE SUM after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a literary assistant who takes dictation or copies manuscripts.
